campingRules.rule: Camping in Abisko National Park is only allowed at designated sites.
designatedSites: STF Abisko Turiststation / main entrance area
Nissonjohka about 5 km south of the main entrance along Kungsleden

campingRules.rule: Hikers with tents who do not want to stay at Abiskojaure must continue a few kilometres beyond Abiskojaure along Kungsleden to leave the national park.

fireRules.rule: Fires and grills are only allowed at designated places in Abisko National Park; camp stoves are permitted.
Temporary fire bans override designated-fireplace availability and must be checked at import/use time.

toiletsAndShelter.details: Wind shelter, benches, fireplaces, firewood and dry toilet reported by Naturkartan facilities pass.
STF hut facilities include guest kitchen, shop and sauna in season; tent site has access to kitchen, sauna and latrine according to Naturkartan facilities pass.

wasteNotes: STF waste management allows some sorted recyclables at huts, but light/portable waste should be carried out.
Assume Nissonjohka has no waste disposal unless field signage or an official site page confirms otherwise.

rules.details: Dogs are generally prohibited in Abisko National Park, but leashed dogs are allowed 1 January-30 April throughout the park and year-round on roads/marked trails including Kungsleden plus near Abisko Turiststation and Abiskojaure cabins.
Hunting and fishing are prohibited; disturbing wildlife, catching insects, taking eggs/nests and similar disturbance are prohibited.
Landing aircraft including drones is prohibited; riding and using motor vehicles outside designated roads, car parks or snowmobile trails is prohibited.

Do not damage ground, blocks, vegetation, living/dead trees or shrubs. Berries and mushrooms may be picked; dry branches/twigs may be collected only within the regulation exception for fire at designated places or shelter.
The marked Abiskojakka delta bird-protection area is closed to visitors 1 May-31 July. This appears near the start/delta area rather than on the normal section through-route, but matters for detours.
Do not disturb grazing reindeer or reindeer-herding work; Abisko is in Gabna sameby area.

The Abisko regulations require permission for certain organized activities, including repeated organized tours/activities and sports events; see regulation PDF before modelling group/event permissions.

currentness.details: No standing closure or reroute for Abisko-Abiskojaure was found on Lanstyrelsen's current mountain info, Abisko park page, or Naturkartan route page as of 2026-04-29. Treat this as no closure found, not a guarantee of open conditions.
Lanstyrelsen notice published/updated 2026-04-22 says trail checks stopped because spring warmth made snow/ice unsafe and fast-changing. Do not present winter/spring travel as checked or reliable.
Lanstyrelsen notice published/updated 2026-03-27 warns of weak ice/open water on mountain lakes and streams, variable snow depth, bare ground/stones and hidden hazards under new snow.
STF lists Abiskojaure 2026 opening periods as 20 February-19 April and 18 June-13 September. On 2026-04-29, the hut/shop is between staffed seasons.

safetyNotes: Use map, compass/GPS and current mountain-weather information; STF says embedded maps are planning tools and should not replace a physical map and compass.
Summer trails are marked with painted poles, stones or trees; winter trails are marked with crosses and may be difficult to follow in summer.
Key crossings/bridges mentioned or implied include Nissunjohka and Kamajakka; no official bridge-by-bridge status was found in this pass.
Mosquitoes, wet ground, early-season snow and high water can affect practical difficulty.

notes: Recent reviews describe the route as moderate, well marked, sometimes busy and sometimes not crowded.
A 2025-07-06 review flags mosquitoes.
A 2025-08-06 review reports a bridge closure making the trail impassable without rerouting, but the bridge is not identified.
A winter review says skis were needed.
conditionReports.importImpact: Treat bridge-closure mention as anecdotal field alert requiring current official confirmation; do not encode as a standing closure.

sourceContradictions.details: STF says 15 km and 4-6 hours; Naturkartan says 14.0 km and 4-5 hours; AllTrails and OSM-derived sources are around 14-15 km. Use STF's 15 km / 4-6 h for official section display, and record 14.0 km Naturkartan linework distance as geometry metadata.
Official descriptions present Abiskojaure hut/cabin as the stage end, while Naturkartan notes hikers leave Kungsleden and cross Kamajakka by suspension bridge to reach the cabins.
sourceContradictions.recommendedTreatment: Use the hut area as the section endpoint for stage UX, but preserve a note that the hut access is a short spur from the through-route so section joins can avoid duplicated geometry.

lanes.summary: Confirmed STF Stage 1 facts, official route description, facility/end coordinates, camping and rule basics.
Found Naturkartan site 12850 linework, OSM relation 6289365, endpoint gap notes, no stable GPX/KML/GeoJSON download.
Identified importable start, mid-section and end facilities with coordinates and import decisions; flagged beach/viewpoint as pending.

Collected recent route-app, blog and forum condition notes; highlighted mosquitoes, crowding, early-season snow/wetness and one unverified bridge-closure report.
Confirmed Abisko National Park restrictions, spring 2026 currentness warnings, and no official section closure found.
